fields.description: Marks, type and print for small studios
Hardbacks and zines, cover to colophon

fields.label: Details
fields.info: One free line: Oil on linen, 120 × 90 cm.

fields.summary: A wordmark cut from one brushstroke, and the signage to carry it.
fields.body:
The studio throws everything by hand, so the mark had to be made the same way: one stroke, no cleanup. We drew it a few hundred times and kept the eleventh.

The signage uses the same stroke at the scale of a doorway, routed into oak and left unpainted.

fields.summary: Letterforms borrowed from the river's old tide tables.
fields.body:
The guesthouse kept a drawer of printed tide tables from the 1950s. Their numerals became the starting point for a small set of letters.

The letters run through the stationery, the room keys and a plain website that reads like a timetable.

fields.summary: A mark that threads itself through every label.
fields.body:
The workshop sells by the metre and by the blanket, so the labels had to work at both sizes.

The mark is one line that passes over and under itself, woven into the cloth labels and printed on the boxes.

fields.summary: Forty dinners, forty drawings, one long table.
fields.body:
A cookbook built around one table and the people who sat at it over a year. Every dinner has a drawing and a page of notes.

The drawings were made on the night, in ink, and printed at the size they were drawn.

fields.summary: A pocket book for a year of Sunday walks.
fields.body:
Fifty-two walks around the city, one for each Sunday, with a map, a route and a blank page for notes.

The book is sized for a coat pocket and printed on paper that takes a pencil.

fields.summary: Everything I know about the coast, in ink.
fields.body:
A small zine about the stretch of coast south of the city, drawn over one summer.

Printed on a risograph in two colours and folded by hand.

fields.summary: Thirty mornings, one window, the same cup.
fields.body:
Every morning for a month I drew the same cup on the same sill before starting work.

The light changed more than the cup did. The drawings hang in the order they were made.

fields.summary: Boats at rest in the Tagus, drawn from the ferry.
fields.body:
Drawn on the morning ferry over a winter, each one finished before the boat docked.

The wash went on later, from memory, in the studio.

fields.summary: Interiors with nobody in them.
fields.body:
Rooms in friends' houses, drawn while they were out.

Each drawing took an afternoon and was left unfinished where the light ran out.

fields.summary: Twelve drawings about rain, hung in a dry room.
fields.body:
A group show about weather, with twelve of my drawings of rain across one wall.

The drawings were hung low, at the height of a child, so you look down into them.

fields.summary: A year of mornings on one wall.
fields.body:
My first solo show: a drawing for every morning of one year, three hundred and sixty-five in a grid.

The grid ran the length of the room and finished at the door.

fields.summary: Drawings made in the margins of other work.
fields.body:
A group show of drawings made beside other jobs: in notebooks, on proofs, on the backs of letters.

My part was a wall of proof sheets with the drawings left where they fell.

fields.info: One of experience, education, exhibition, award, press, talk.

fields.note: Identity systems and books for small makers
Books, posters and the occasional wall

entries.title: A page of ink before anything else

fields.author: Juno Reyes
fields.standfirst: Why every project starts with a drawing, even the websites.
fields.image_alt: A page of ink before anything else
fields.body:
Every project here started as a page of ink. Before type, before a grid, I draw the thing I am trying to say until the shape is obvious.

The drawings are rarely used as they are. They set the proportions, the weight and the mood, and the design follows them. When a client sees the ink first, the conversation is about the idea, not the software.

This is why the studio keeps a long table and north light. Most mornings begin there, and the screens wait until the afternoon.

fields.author: Juno Reyes
fields.standfirst: Forty drawings, one spine, a week at the bindery.
fields.body:
The book was bound by hand at a small bindery north of the river. I spent a week there folding and watching.

The spine is cloth, the boards are bare, and every copy smells faintly of glue.

entries.title: Why I draw the same cup

fields.author: Juno Reyes
fields.standfirst: On repetition as a way of seeing.
fields.image_alt: Why I draw the same cup
fields.body:
The cup has not changed in three years. The drawings of it have.

Drawing one thing over and over is the best way I know to stop seeing what I expect.

fields.author: Juno Reyes
fields.standfirst: North light, a heater, and the long table.
fields.body:
In winter the light in the studio is flat and grey and very good for drawing.

The heater is loud, the table is long, and most days nobody else comes up the stairs.

fields.author: Juno Reyes
fields.standfirst: Hanging a year of mornings on one wall.
fields.body:
Three hundred and sixty-five drawings take two days to hang. We did it in order, January at the window.

The hardest part was the gaps: the days I missed are on the wall too, as blank frames.

entries.title: Zines I keep coming back to

fields.author: Juno Reyes
fields.standfirst: Six small books that taught me more than the big ones.
fields.image_alt: Zines I keep coming back to
fields.body:
A short list of zines that live on the shelf above my desk.

None of them is longer than thirty-two pages, and every one of them was folded by its maker.

/privacy.title: Privacy
/privacy.content:
This site keeps a note in your browser that you have seen the cookie notice, and nothing else. The contact form sends your name, email and message to me and to no one else.

What is kept

Messages are kept for as long as the conversation lasts, then deleted. Write to hello@junoreyes.example to have yours removed sooner.
